en: So we can chat with Ollama. That's pretty
straightforward.
There are 2 important features about this
chat which I wanna highlight here.
One is related to multiline messages because
right now if I type something here like hi
and I then wanna enter a new line to
structure my input, for example,
if I hit enter, I just send this as a
message,
which might not always be what I wanna do.
So in order to send multiline messages, you
can and should use triple double quotes.
Then if you hit Enter, you don't send the
message, but you enter a new line.
So here I could now
write a message like this, and you then end
with triple double quotes again.
So opening and closing triple double quotes,
and in between your multiline message.
And this will then send the message.
So that's one important thing.
What's also important is that when dealing
with a vision model, which Gemma 3 is,
you can of course not just use it to handle
text input, but also image input. Gemma 3
models and a couple of other models as well
are able to extract information from images.
Now you can of course use Ollama
programmatically to send images to it, and
that is something we'll explore later in
this section. But you can also use an image
here in the chat.
And to do that, all you have to do is type
your prompt like, what's on this image?
And then
separated with a space, you provide a path
to that image.
In my case, it's an image called max.jpg,
which sits in the same folder as I'm
currently in.
So I provide a relative path to that image
starting with./
You could also have an absolute path here to
the image that might be stored somewhere
else on your system.
And now if I send this, Ollama detects that
I added an image to the prompt. And for it
to detect that, your image path must come
last after your prompt. The order is
important.
And it now sent this image along with my
prompt to Ollama. And therefore here,
I get a nice output
describing what's on the image, that it's a
man
in a recording setup
and that there is a thumbs up gesture.
And that is correct because this here is the
image I sent to Ollama. It's this Max JPEG
file.
So if you are working with a multimodal
model like the Gemma 3 model, which is not
just capable of handling text but also
images, you can send both to it. It's just
the order that's important.
